name: b-returns-after-failover
description: SIMULATED SETTING, not a measurement: link delays are configured so that A-B and B-C (10 ms one way) are cheaper than A-D and D-C (25 ms one way). B stops at 10 s, A fails over to D, and the controller confirms A > D > C. B returns at 20 s. Nothing switches back by itself: A keeps using D until the controller, after the hold-down and because the simulated B links are cheaper, installs a route through B.
